A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CREward study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched, including v1 Appendix D becoming v2 Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original human preference evaluations, LVLM alignment measurements, backbone comparisons, and quantitative and qualitative LoRA experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on unseen synthetic objects and real ImageNet images.

M1.justification: The frozen vision backbone, five-layer reward head, pairwise learning objective, and type-specific LoRA procedure are retained. Expanded explanations and renaming the prompt variable from y to p do not change the method.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds evaluation on real images from 40 object-centric ImageNet-1k classes, substantially extending the previously synthetic-image coverage. It also adds a separate reward-alignment test on five objects unseen during training; v1 already included unseen-object LoRA generation experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same LVLMs, Surprise metric, vision backbones, ConceptLab/C3 comparisons, and prompting baselines. The new generalization study measures agreement with the already-used Gemma model.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces 1,000 randomly sampled pairs from 5,000 synthetic images and exhaustive 15-by-15 comparisons between top- and bottom-ranked ImageNet images. Section 3.3 also removes the statement about generating equally many ordinary images, without establishing that the creative-image training pairs or existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds targeted checks of reward alignment under unseen-object and synthetic-to-real distribution shifts, accompanied by top/bottom examples. Existing slider-strength, negative-direction, mixed-slider, identity-preservation, and Grad-CAM analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing standard-deviation reporting is unchanged. Figure H includes additional ± values for new results, but specifies no new repeated-run design, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Figure H reports geometry/material/texture/overall preference alignment of 0.80/0.80/0.77/0.80 on unseen synthetic objects and 0.63/0.46/0.75/0.83 on ImageNet, plus qualitative examples. These are additional results under new conditions; retained tables and experimental findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The reward-learning equations, LoRA objectives, and supplementary derivation are unchanged. Explicitly explaining the existing winning-rate calculation and changing prompt notation add no new mathematical definition or reasoning.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds a qualified claim that the approach generalizes to some unseen scenarios, referring to Appendix D. The central novelty claim, human-alignment claims, and three application areas remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly leaves multi-object settings and noisy environments for future work. Appendix D attributes weaker ImageNet alignment to its lack of creativity-focused curation. Existing limitations concerning semantic value and entangled creativity types are retained in condensed wording.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a project link for code and dataset access. Appendix D documents its image source and pair-sampling procedures. Existing architecture, training hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Creative Blends of Visual Concepts and CREA, extending discussion to compositional creativity and agent-based refinement. It further emphasizes the limited exploration of control over distinct creative visual aspects.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies annotation and winning-rate explanations, adds specific appendix cross-references, condenses the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments. The principal section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure H with generalization scores and examples, while the previous Figure H becomes Figure I. It updates overview arrows and image presentation, relocates retained tables and Figure 8, and preserves the overall visual organization.

improvement.justification: The new generalization experiments provide useful evidence beyond v1's synthetic-image evaluations, while the access link and explicit applicability limits improve usability and scope transparency. The gain is limited because the added validation relies on Gemma agreement and the ImageNet test selects extreme-ranked pairs; the core method and existing human-validation results remain unchanged.
